_note: THE HOUSE PALETTE, AUTHORED — not extracted. It used to be 32 colours k-means'd out of the LimeZu sheets, which was right while LimeZu was the art. It is not any more: docs/ART_STYLE.md picks muted daylight, and a palette sampled from a pack we are retiring cannot deliver that. Quantising the bright generated tilesets through the old one made the grass MORE saturated, because conform matches a palette and cannot shift one, and the nearest entry to a bright green was a bright green.
_coverage: COVERAGE MATTERS MORE THAN TASTE HERE. A quantiser sends every pixel to its nearest entry, so a region with no entry lands somewhere absurd — session 3 lost a day to an explosion turning magenta because there was no saturated red anywhere between hue 20 and 40, and the fix was sampling a wider source rather than reweighting the distance metric. So every family below is deliberate and none may be dropped for looking dull on its own: pasture, earth, straw, timber, barn red, dusk sky, skin and cloth, the cursed greens, and neutrals.
_cursed: The last family is the horror one and it is the reason this file is authored rather than pretty. Cursed art is grey-green rot with sickly yellow eyes (ART_STYLE.md), and those greens must be DISTINCT from the healthy pasture greens or a diseased animal quantises straight back into a healthy one.
_regenerating: `npm run conform -- --write` still extracts a palette from the packs and WILL overwrite this file. That is no longer the source of truth; it is a reference tool. If you run it, diff before committing.
_order: Sorted roughly by lightness within family. Order is not load-bearing — the quantiser searches all of them.
